guide.title: Mount Eustis Ski Hill, New Hampshire: Littleton's rope tow, reopened after 32 years
guide.intro: The rope tow at Mount Eustis was formally dedicated by the Littleton Outing Club on January 28 or 29, 1939, per the New England Lost Ski Areas Project's page on Mount Eustis. The Town of Littleton purchased the land in 1960, acquiring 34.67 acres for $7,200, and continued to operate the area until about 1983, "although the exact last day of skiing is not yet known," per the same source.

sections.heading: The 32-year reopening
sections.body: A nonprofit, Mt. Eustis Ski Hill, was organized in 2013, allowing for formal fundraising toward reopening the hill, per NELSAP's page. The 2013 fundraising plan called for a rehabilitated rope tow from the former ski area in Lisbon, NH, to be restored by Littleton High School students, per the same page. Mt. Eustis held its official grand opening on February 7, 2015; on that day, per NELSAP, the donated rope tow had generator trouble, and snowmobiles were used to bring skiers to the summit. NELSAP's own page describes the reopening as holding "the record for the longest closed ski area to reopen in New England - approximately 32 years." Mount Eustis Ski Hill's own website states the hill is now "powered entirely by a passionate volunteer crew and the non-profit's dedicated board of directors."

sections.heading: In Littleton
sections.body: Schilling Beer Co. operates a Brewery Pub & Kitchen at 18 Mill St in Littleton, NH, in addition to a separate Store & Tasting Room and Mill St. Kitchen on the same street, per the brewery's own website. Chutters describes its Littleton store, per its own website, as "Home of the World's Longest Candy Counter," stating the counter runs 112 feet along the store. The Littleton Diner's own site states the original diner car was "built in Merrimack, MA in 1928 and transported to Littleton, NH - where it opened in 1930," and that "in 1940 a new Sterling Diner was constructed on the original site." Thayers Inn describes itself on its own site as "a historic New England landmark" with "Greek revival architecture," positioned as the central hub of downtown Littleton. A bronze Pollyanna statue in front of the Littleton public library was unveiled in 2002 by the citizens of Littleton in honor of author Eleanor H. Porter, one of the town's most famous residents, per Wikipedia's "Pollyanna" article.

faq.question: Why did Mount Eustis Ski Hill close and reopen?
faq.answer: The Town of Littleton operated the area until about 1983. A nonprofit, Mt. Eustis Ski Hill, was organized in 2013 to raise funds toward reopening it, and the hill held its official grand opening on February 7, 2015 -- what NELSAP describes as "the record for the longest closed ski area to reopen in New England - approximately 32 years."

faq.question: Who runs Mount Eustis Ski Hill today?
faq.answer: Mount Eustis Ski Hill's own website states the hill is "powered entirely by a passionate volunteer crew and the non-profit's dedicated board of directors."
